topic: Your power side-mirror won't move — switch, motor, or fuse?
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: Your side mirror stopped moving — and the buttons don't do anything.
beats.visualPrompt: Exterior close-up on a car's side mirror housing, static camera, driver reaching toward the door-panel switch out of frame, soft daylight, shallow depth of field.

beats.narration: No motor sound, no click, nothing. Could be one mirror, or both.
beats.visualPrompt: Interior shot of a door-panel mirror-adjust switch/joystick, static mount, subtle backlight glow on the switch icon, no hand pressing it in frame.

beats.narration: One clue: it's usually the switch, the mirror motor, or a blown fuse — three different fixes.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro/cutaway shot: a small electric mirror-adjust motor assembly removed and resting on a workbench, slow push-in, no hands or tools visible in frame.

beats.narration: If only one side is dead, that narrows it fast. If neither moves, check the fuse first.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a vehicle fuse box panel, one fuse slot highlighted/illuminated, dim garage lighting, static mounted camera.

beats.narration: Don't guess which part it is. A quick check can point to the actual cause.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a multimeter probe resting clipped against a wiring connector near a mirror harness, shop bay softly blurred in the background, no hand holding the meter.

beats.narration: Worth checking before you order the wrong part. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.
beats.visualPrompt: Branded end-card plate: Nick's Tire & Auto shop bay wide shot, warm daylight, static hold. Logo and CTA text composited in post, never AI-generated.
